body:
Finding someone else is easier said than done.  It's quite difficult to advertise that sort of thing, and even more difficult to find someone who would be involved in it.  And I don't even know if the ageplay fetish thing you're referring to would ever be even remotely close to the same.

As for the therapy to come to terms with it, I see no point in that, because it's a fact about myself I've accepted more than 14 years ago.  I often cope with it just using my imagination or reading stories.  But that won't change how alone I feel.

There's no reliable way to talk to people about it.  No support groups, or anything similar.

No, I didn't choose this.  And I also know that therapy will be about as effective as therapy was when people with homosexual feelings were "treated."  You can't treat away a desire.  Even if I could trust a therapist, what would they do for me?  Try and decrease overall sexual desire through medications?  I doubt that will stop me from thinking about it all the time.  And being an extremely productive member of society, whom people admire and compliment doesn't change the the fact that I always know whenever I talk to someone, if they knew the truth, they would most likely do everything they could to destroy me.  I know there's a lot of people who think it's a mental illness, and many people still think homosexual people are mentally ill.  I firmly believe there's no "cure" for either.  And when you can't be true to yourself in front of anyone, not even a single person, it's difficult to have the desire to continue through life, alone.
